label: s-initial sequence, u/b in the last two inputs, at step 3-4 (boosted by j)
explanation: Very sparse conjunctive detector for a specific original-phase prefix. Almost all activations (99.7% of mass) fall at original steps t=3-4 of sequences whose first token is s (90% of mass), where one or both of the previous two inputs are u or b. Input j at that step strongly boosts it: the top examples are all s,u/b,u/b,[j] (max on s u b j). Without j, it fires weakly when both previous inputs are u/b (e.g. s u u [v], s u b [t]). Does not fire in the copy phase, at t<3 or t>=5, or on j/u/b contexts without a leading s. The coarse context alone (s first, t=3-4, u/b nearby) has ~87% mass recall but only ~4% precision, so the feature needs a finer combination than the predicate captures. Dev F1 0.62, mass recall 0.85.
